topic: Static, dynamic and total pressure, principle of A.S.I, Indicated, rectified, equivalent and true air speed, errors in A.S.I.
syllabus_extract: Static, dynamic and total pressure, principle of A.S.I, Indicated, rectified, equivalent and true air speed, errors in A.S.I.
specific_objectives: 6.1.1.1 Trainee will be able to explain the properties of atmosphere, flow over bodies, boundary layer.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Demonstration of Pitot-Static probe installation and error sources; Safety: Ensure probe is disconnected before handling; Supervision: Instructor monitors probe alignment and trainee safety during setup.
intro_questions: What is the definition of static pressure?
How does dynamic pressure relate to airspeed?
Can you define total pressure in the context of flight?

development.content:
Definition of Static Pressure
Definition of Dynamic Pressure
Definition of Total Pressure
Bernoulli's Principle Application
Pitot-Static System Components

Indicated Airspeed (IAS)
Rectified Airspeed (CAS)
Equivalent Airspeed (EAS)
True Airspeed (TAS)
Relationship between IAS and TAS

Position Error in A.S.I.
Instrument Error in A.S.I.
Compressibility Error
Temperature Error
Correction Factors for Errors

summary_questions: Explain the difference between Indicated and True Airspeed.
List three common sources of error in an Airspeed Indicator.
How does altitude affect the relationship between IAS and TAS?
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on how the principles of static and dynamic pressure apply to the next lesson on streamline and stream tube definitions.

pft_rows.syllabus: Definition of streamline, stream tube, stream filament, ideal and real fluid, steady and turbulent flow, compressible and incompressible flow, viscous and in viscous flow, rotational and irrotational flow.
